newsitem.title: INDIA: India party leader assures support to Gujral rule.
newsitem.headline: India party leader assures support to Gujral rule.

text.p: The leader of Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's Janata Dal party said on Thursday that he would not withdraw support for the government despite deep leadership differences that threaten to split the party.

"My supporters will not pull down the Gujral government under any circumstance," Laloo Prasad Yadav, whose backers plan to hold a rebel convention on Saturday, told reporters. Yadav's group boycotted voting for the party's presidency on Thursday.
Leaders of the Janata Dal, the largest group in Gujral's 15-party United Front coalition, voted on Thursday for the first time in the party's nine years of existence to select their leaders.

But Yadav alleged that party voter lists had been rigged against him and he called on his supporters to boycott the polling. Results of the balloting in the main faction were not expected before Sunday.

The convention on Saturday in New Delhi was expected to result in a split in the Janata Dal which leads the centre-left government. Yadav, a powerful low-caste leader is said to command 16 Janata Dal lawmakers out of 45. The ruling minority alliance, of which Janata Dal is part, has 178 members in the 545-seat lower house of parliament, the Lok Sabha.
Laloo Yadav's differences were said to be essentially with former prime minister Deve Gowda.
